title: Beyond the 956: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, historic leader of Mexico's left and three-time presidential candidate, dies at 92
excerpt: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, the historic leader of Mexico's left, founder of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) and three-time presidential candidate, has died at 92. El Universal confirmed the death through sources close to the family; he died on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas Solórzano, the historic leader of Mexico's left, founder of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) and three-time presidential candidate, has died at 92.

Cárdenas died on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, El Universal reported, confirming the death through sources close to the family. Milenio and El País also reported his death on Wednesday. No cause of death had been publicly reported at the time of publication.

Born on May 1, 1934, in Mexico City, Cárdenas was the son of former President Lázaro Cárdenas del Río. He studied civil engineering at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) before entering public life.

He served as a senator for Michoacán from 1976 to 1980 and as governor of Michoacán from 1980 to 1986. In 1987, he broke with the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), leading the Democratic Current movement that challenged the party's internal candidate-selection process.

In 1988, he ran for president at the head of the National Democratic Front, in an election marked by the so-called “fall of the system” and allegations of electoral irregularities. The following year, in 1989, he helped found the PRD, which became one of Mexico's principal left-wing opposition forces.

Cárdenas ran for president again in 1994 and in 2000. In 1997, he became the first head of government of the then-Federal District elected by popular vote, serving until 1999 — a milestone in Mexico's democratic transition.

President Claudia Sheinbaum paid tribute to him as “a man of firm principles, who transformed the political life of our country,” adding that his dignity and republican conviction remain an essential reference for the nation. Former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador called him a precursor of Mexico's democratic movement.

Sources: El Universal (via sources close to the family); Milenio; El País; statements by President Claudia Sheinbaum and former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador.
